project: C:\Portfolio — "cinematic scroll-film" portfolio for Theodore Von Joshua (Full Stack AI Engineer). It copies the style of hyowonbernabe.me but uses its own code. The page is a fixed 1920x1080 stage scaled to the window. 24 "shots" (scenes) are scrubbed by scroll on paused GSAP timelines, with resting frames where the scroll holds. Layered on top: HUD corner brackets, film grain, a red cursor ring, a star particle field, and a procedural three.js pistol that travels between scenes (with an exploded view and per-part skills). Scenes change colour with iris floods between colour fields. Files: index.html, css/style.css, js/main.js (the engine), js/content.js (all copy), js/scenes/{util,boot,about,arsenal,projects,index}.js, js/gun.js. The spec is CONTRACT.md. There is only one git commit.
stack: Static ES modules with no build step, served by python -m http.server. Libraries load from jsDelivr as globals: gsap@3.12.5 (core only, no ScrollTrigger; scroll is mapped to time by hand), lenis@1.1.13 (smooth scroll, driven manually through lenis.raf), d3-geo@3.1.1 + topojson-client@3.1.0 for the globe scene, and three@0.160.0 through an import map. Plain JS, no TypeScript, no framework. Fonts are Geist (400/600/900) and Geist Mono (400/600/700) from Google Fonts. Porting to Vite only needs `npm i gsap lenis three` and `import gsap from 'gsap'`. Nothing in the code depends on the CDN.
visual_signature:
PALETTE: a hard four-colour poster system with almost no greys. Tokens: --ink #050505 (near-black base), --red #ff0f0f (pure signal red, used as a whole background field as well as an accent), --bone #ededed (off-white field and text), --blood #4a0000 (deep red, used once in the quad cells), --ash #8a8585 (muted mono labels). A fifth near-black, #0b0b0b, is used for one quad cell. Each scene is a full flat field of one colour (ink, red or bone), and text inverts to suit: ink on red or bone, bone on ink. On red fields the red accents turn ink, so accents never vanish. The only glow is red box-shadow on red elements (for example `0 0 17px var(--red)`, or `0 0 27px var(--red), 0 0 58px rgba(255,15,15,.6)`). There are no gradients except a repeating-linear-gradient for tick rulers. TYPE: display is Geist 900, uppercase, very tight tracking. Sizes: .mega is 250px with line-height .84 and letter-spacing -.045em; .big is 150px/.9 at -.04em; .mid is 84px/.95 at -.03em; the hero name is 290px; showcase titles are 180px; a ghost numeral runs to 1100px. Labels use Geist Mono 600/700, uppercase, with wide tracking (.18em to .34em) at 12 to 22px. Body copy is rare: Geist 600 at 34px/1.3. Outline type `.ol` (-webkit-text-fill-color: transparent; -webkit-text-stroke: 3px currentColor) is mixed into solid headlines ("00 and counting", "LET'S
    TALK
"). Headlines end in a red full stop (".", or a round `.period` dot in the type colour) such as "Certified." and "LOADED." The full stop doubles as an animation object, swelling to flood the screen. SPACING: everything is absolutely positioned in stage px. Side margins are 90 to 130px (100 or 130 is typical), with 1660 to 1720px content widths, 3px rules across the full content width, 2 to 3px solid borders, and no border-radius on cards (sharp and brutalist). Only the phone mock and dots are round. WHAT MAKES IT FEEL NON-TEMPLATE: (1) It is a film, not a scrolling page. A fixed stage plays scenes with authored timings and hard field cuts. (2) Military and terminal fiction carries the content: biometric scan, ACCESS GRANTED, ammo pips, gun parts as skill groups, "LOADED.", "DEPLOYED", a match-probability counter. (3) Editorial meta corners like "Portfolio / 2026" and "N° 001 / Hero", act labels "05 · Projects", and numbered "01 / 04" counters. (4) Brutalist hover offset shadows `box-shadow:10px 10px 0 rgba(5,5,5,.55)`. (5) Rotating 22-point seal-star badges. (6) Strike-through red bars over "pain words". (7) Grain over everything at opacity .1.

effects.name: Scroll-to-film-time mapping with hold frames (no ScrollTrigger)
effects.how: Each scene has a paused gsap.timeline whose length equals its dur, padded with tl.set({}, {}, dur). Scenes are laid end to end on a global time axis (t0 is cumulative). Scroll px are built as segments {y0,y1,t0,t1}: a scene gets SCENE_PX(850) * clamp(dur/2.5, .8, 1.7) px. If the scene has a `rest`, its segment is split at restAt and a HOLD_PX(800) segment with t0 == t1 is inserted, so the film freezes while the user keeps scrolling. In each rAF: lenis.raf(now); t = scrollToTime(lenis.scroll). Then the active scene is found, given the class .on (visibility visible) and set with tl.totalTime(t - s.t0, false). Lenis setup: new Lenis({lerp:.085, smoothWheel:!reducedMotion, wheelMultiplier:.9, touchMultiplier:1.4}). It is stopped during the intro and started after it.

effects.name: Autoplay intro gated on asset load
effects.how: html.locked { overflow:hidden }. The film clock autoplays t += dt until GATE_T (scan at 97%) while the 3D model loads, then runs to the landing rest frame (REST_T). At that point the class is removed, lenis.start() and lenis.scrollTo(0,{immediate:true}). A safety setTimeout of 15s forces ready. Under reduced motion it jumps straight to REST_T. The first frame waits on Promise.race([document.fonts.ready, 2.5s timeout]).

effects.name: Iris flood transitions between colour fields
effects.how: When a scene's ending field differs from the next scene's start field, main.js appends a 4500px div.iris (position absolute, border-radius 50%, left/top at the iris point, negative margins of half its size, background = next field colour, z-index 30). It tweens scale .02 to 1 with ease power3.in over the last 0.55s of the scene. #viewport background switches to the next colour 0.25s before the end. For in-scene turns, the scene places its own iris and flips text colour with tl.set(el,{color},t). The hero variant hides the iris inside the full stop: a round span .16em wide holds a 3400px circle scaled to (fontSize*.16)/3400, pops in with back.out(3), then scales to 1 to flood the frame in ink.

effects.name: Masked line reveal
effects.how: Markup: LINE, styled .mask{overflow:hidden;display:block;padding:.06em 0;margin:-.06em 0}. The padding keeps descenders and the tight leading uncut. Animation: tl.from('.mask > span', {yPercent:110..118, duration:.8-.95, ease:'power4.out' or 'expo.out', stagger:.14}).

effects.name: Deterministic scramble decode (scrub-safe)
effects.how: Tweens a proxy {p} from 0 to 1. In onUpdate, step = floor(p*24). Each char i is final once p >= (i+1)/n; until then it is GLYPHS[floor(hash(i*7+step)*len)], using the sin-hash instead of Math.random so it reverses cleanly. Used for ACCESS GRANTED and IDENTITY CONFIRMED.

effects.name: Scrub-safe counters
effects.how: count(tl, fn, from, to, at, dur, ease) tweens a proxy {v} with immediateRender:false and calls fn(v) onUpdate. Values are zero-padded with pad(). The '00 AND COUNTING' project count works this way, as do the 97% match and the 142 minutiae.

effects.name: Film grain
effects.how: A 256x256 canvas is filled with random grey noise and turned into a data URL, used as the background-image of a fixed #grain at 300% x 300% (130% on touch), z-index 50, opacity .1. The CSS animation grainJitter 1.2s steps(8) infinite translates it between keyframes like (-6%,-8%) and (-12%,-18%).

effects.name: Custom cursor ring
effects.how: body{cursor:none}. #cursor is 32px with a 1.5px red border, plus an outline of 1px rgba(5,5,5,.85) so it reads on red. ::before adds an inset bone 1px ring and ::after a 4px red centre dot with stacked ink and bone rings. A cursorPulse 2s animation runs the glow between 5px and 15px. Movement uses gsap.quickTo(cursor,'x',{duration:.15,ease:'power2.out'}). On pointerover a or .chip it tweens scale 1.9 (.25s power3.out), returning to 1 on pointerout. Hidden on (pointer:coarse).

effects.name: Cursor-repelled star field
effects.how: A fixed canvas sits behind transparent 'starry' ink scenes. Star count ≈ w*h*170/(1920*1080), clamped to 60..320. Each star has x, y, a drifting dx/dy (dy slightly negative, so stars drift up), target alpha .1-.7 and radius .6 or 1.6. Within R=140 of the mouse, push force = ((R-d)/R)^2*25/50 along the angle away from the cursor; otherwise the offset decays by 1/50 per frame. Stars that leave the screen respawn at the bottom edge. The canvas opacity fades .4s and drawing stops 0.7s after the stars are unwanted.

effects.name: HUD tone switching and ammo pips
effects.how: Each frame computes the field (accounting for a mid-scene turn) and toggles .light on #hud, #ammo and #act for red or bone fields, and .off for the quad scene. Text colour transitions .2s. The per-scene ammo count (0-3) sets .on on the pips. #act text comes from the scene's act label.

effects.name: SVG fingerprint draw plus clipped red scan
effects.how: 24 elliptical ring paths, each with a deterministic gap and slight sin wobble, use pathLength=1 and stroke-dasharray=1, animated with from strokeDashoffset:1 at stagger .035. The base copy is bone at .26 opacity. A red copy sits in a clipPath rect whose attr height tweens 0 to 660 in sync with a glowing 4px scanline moving y 0 to 660.

effects.name: Collapse to the dot
effects.how: The whole content group (transform-origin at the centre) tweens scaleY 1 to .012 (power3.in, .5s), then scaleX to 0 (.42s), then opacity 0. A red dot pops scale 0 to 1.9 to 1, two rings expand from scale .1 to 9 and 6 while fading, and crosshair lines draw in with scaleX/scaleY.

effects.name: Rotating seal badge
effects.how: A 22-point star polygon (radii alternate 98 and 83 in a 200 viewBox) with red fill and centred text (a 76px 900 big word plus a small mono line). It enters from scale 0 at rotation -140 with back.out(1.7), and the svg alone spins rotation 0 to 260 linearly across the scene duration, so it is scrub-linked.

effects.name: Hover states (cards, rows, links)
effects.how: Cards invert fill to ink with color bone and get box-shadow 10px 10px 0 rgba(5,5,5,.55). The arrow translates (5px,-5px) over .25s. Contact rows invert to ink and padding-left goes 24 to 46px. Link underline: border-bottom 2px red, padding-bottom 10px, mono 20px with .2em tracking. focus-visible: outline 3px red, outline-offset 4px, plus box-shadow 0 0 0 8px ink.

effects.name: 3D pistol with exploded skills
effects.how: A procedural low-poly model (boxes and cylinders) uses MeshStandardMaterial gunmetal plus bone EdgesGeometry(geo,25) outlines (LineBasicMaterial opacity .5), a red PointLight(RED,70) that follows the mouse, and a transparent background. Shared pose state {px,py,rx,ry,rz,s,ex} is tweened by the timelines through makePoser, so each scene's pose continues from the previous one. ex drives part.position = base + dir*ex. Hovering a part sets red emissive and shows a fixed skills panel beside the cursor, with a red ring projected onto the part's screen position. Optional to port; a crypto equivalent might be a coin or candle object.

standing_rules: From CONTRACT.md. Every scroll-linked tween must be reversible and scrub-safe: only tl.from, fromTo, to and set. Do not use tl.call for visual state, timers, Math.random or Date inside timelines; use the sin-hash for deterministic pseudo-randomness. Start states come from from/fromTo, never from CSS hidden states.
Text reveals always use .mask > span with a yPercent animation (110-118), never a plain fade.

Every link is a real <a href target="_blank" rel="noopener">, and mailto links have no target. No dummy or # links. Only <a> and .chip receive pointer events inside scenes (.scene * {pointer-events:none}).
Quality bar: a premium dark, red and bone editorial film. Margins of at least 90px. No overflow or overlapping text. Type stays legible when the stage is scaled to about 0.6. No console errors.
Keep each file under about 700 lines. Each file has one owner and a clear module interface. Content and copy live in a single content.js data file ('replace values, nothing else needs to change').

Accessibility: respect prefers-reduced-motion (no smooth wheel, no star drift or cursor push, jump straight to the rest frame, panel transitions shortened). Decorative layers get aria-hidden. A visually hidden #about-text holds a full plain-text copy of all content for screen readers and SEO. Each scene has role=region and an aria-label. A <noscript> message is provided. focus-visible gets a 3px red outline with offset 4. Chips have tabindex 0 and open their panel on keyboard focus.

Mobile and touch: on (pointer: coarse), hide the custom cursor and restore cursor:auto, shrink the grain to 130%, cap the 3D pixel ratio at .75-1.25, and use tap (under 12px movement, under 600ms) instead of hover.

Perf: draw loops skip work when hidden (stars stop 0.7s after they are off). Only DOM properties that changed are updated (lastField, lastTone and similar caches). DPR is capped at 2. Every subsystem is wrapped in try/catch with console.error so one failure never kills the film. Heavy assets load async with a safety timeout so the intro can never hang.

Pin exact CDN versions (gsap@3.12.5, lenis@1.1.13, three@0.160.0) and preconnect to fonts and the CDN. The favicon is an inline SVG data-URI (an ink square with a red dot). theme-color is set to the ink colour, plus color-scheme dark.

From the user's global CLAUDE.md, which overrides this reference: no hyphens or dashes before text and no decorative leading rules before labels. The Portfolio's .eyebrow::before 56px rule and the pj-eb::before rule must NOT be ported. Write labels as plain text ('05 · PROJECTS' is fine; '—— WHO WE ARE' is not). Avoid em dashes in UI copy; content.js has '2021 — 2025', so use '2021 to 2025' or '2021 · 2025' instead.

Copy voice: terse uppercase, military and terminal metaphor (ACCESS GRANTED, LOADED., DEPLOYED, 'Clearance level 04 · session open'). The middot ' · ' is the separator everywhere (act labels, metadata). Headlines end with a full stop, and numbers are zero-padded (01, 001).

Most visitors arrive through Facebook/Instagram in-app browsers on mid-range Philippine phones over slow connections. Key files: C:\GN Ventures\GN  Tech Run\CLAUDE.md (binding spec), CONTRACT.md (file ownership, DOM IDs, module init order), index.html, vite.config.js, event.config.json, src\main.js, src\styles\{tokens,base,sections,motion,bg,cursor}.css, src\effects\{splash,reveal,carousel,sfx,background3d,three-subset}.js, src\features\{config,tracking,countdown,calendar,share,stickyBar,videoModal}.js, src\lib\utm.js.
stack: Vite with vanilla ES modules and plain CSS (no React, Next or Tailwind). Three.js is the only runtime dependency of note. It is tree-shaken through a named re-export file (src/effects/three-subset.js) and lazy-loaded with dynamic import(). Two custom Vite plugins live in vite.config.js. (1) html-tokens: at transformIndexHtml 'pre' it replaces {{dotted.path}} in index.html with values from event.config.json plus img.* from src/generated/images.json, HTML-escapes them, drops any tag carrying data-if="path" when that value is empty, and warns at build about empty keys. (2) inline-css: at generateBundle post it swaps the built <link rel=stylesheet> for an inline <style> so no CSS blocks render. build target es2020, cssCodeSplit false, assetsInlineLimit 0. An asset pipeline (scripts/optimize-assets.mjs with sharp) writes AVIF and WebP at 480/768/1080/1600 widths (hero) or 480/800/1200 (gallery) plus images.json { hero:{src,avifSrcset,webpSrcset,width,height,alt}, gallery:[...], placeholder:bool }. Fonts are self-hosted Poppins WOFF2. Deployed on Vercel from main, with vercel.json setting immutable caching for /assets, 30-day caching for fonts/img/cursor, and strict security headers including a CSP.
visual_signature: Restrained palette, strictly one hue plus white. The full palette is white and shades of blue as CSS custom properties: --white #FFFFFF, --blue-50 #F0F7FF, --blue-100 #DCEBFF, --blue-200 #B9D7FF, --blue-400 #4F9BFF (decoration only, fails AA on white), --blue-600 #1D6FE8 (accent and primary button), --blue-800 #0B3A8C (soft text, hover), --blue-950 #061C47 (ink, splash bg, hero overlay, theme-color). On top sit semantic aliases: --text, --text-soft, --surface, --surface-alt, --border, --accent. Translucent panels come from color-mix(in srgb, var(--white) 86%, transparent) with color-mix borders, used instead of backdrop blur. Shadows are tinted with the brand hue (0 8px 24px rgba(11,58,140,.18)), never neutral black. Type is a single family, Poppins, self-hosted at 400/600/700 only. Headings are 700 at line-height 1.15 with text-wrap: balance. The h1 is clamp(2rem, 11vw, 4.5rem) and section titles clamp(1.5rem, 7vw, 2.5rem), both with white-space: nowrap so titles sit on one line at 360px. Body is 16px at line-height 1.65, prose max-width 62ch with text-wrap: pretty. Nothing goes below 14px (0.875rem), and small labels are 600 uppercase with letter-spacing .04em, not light gray. Buttons are pill-shaped (radius 999px), 48px tall (--btn-h 3rem) with 600 weight, and press down to scale(.98). Cards use radius 14px, inner elements 10px. The spacing scale is 0.25/0.5/0.75/1/1.5/2/3rem. Easing is one curve everywhere, cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1). The non-template feel comes from: a full-bleed photo hero with the title anchored bottom-left over a brand-ink gradient (vertical on mobile, horizontal left-to-right on desktop), a fixed WebGL particle wave field drifting behind translucent white panels, a brand-colored splash on every load, synthesized click ticks with a mute toggle in the header, a custom native CSS cursor, and very tight page length (4 to 5 mobile screens). The structure is merged sections rather than many stacked bands, and photos move sideways, never stacked vertically.
layout_patterns: Sticky translucent header: position sticky, height calc(var(--header-h 3.5rem) + env(safe-area-inset-top)), background color-mix(white 88%), 1px bottom border. Brand logos sit left (1.5rem tall, 2rem from 400px up). The right side holds an icon mute toggle (48px round icon-btn) and a small pill Register button with white-space: nowrap.

Full-bleed photo hero: section.hero is position relative with isolation isolate, display flex and align-items flex-end, so content hugs the bottom. min-height is calc(100svh - header - safe-top), capped at min(46rem, ...) from 900px. <picture> is absolutely positioned at z-index -2 with object-fit cover and object-position 70% (75% on desktop). The ::after overlay at z-index -1 is linear-gradient(to top, ink .95, ink .78 at 45%, ink .4) on mobile and switches to linear-gradient(to right, ink .94, .8 at 40%, .15) on desktop with content max-width 36rem. Content is a grid with gap .75rem: one-line h1, a meta line (date, a CSS middle-dot separator via #hero-date:not(:empty)+#hero-venue:not(:empty)::before{content:'\00B7\00A0'}, venue), a one-line pitch, a two-button row (flex 1 1 9rem, max 16rem), and a one-line tabular-nums countdown.

About merged with event details: one translucent panel (bg color-mix white 86%, 1px border, radius 14px) holding the h2, 2 to 3 sentences, a details-grid, and an action row. details-grid is repeat(2, minmax(0,1fr)) on mobile and repeat(4,...) from 900px. .detail-card--wide spans the full row on mobile and 2 columns on desktop. Each card has an uppercase 14px label and a 600-weight value, and empty values show 'To be announced' in a regular weight. Lists inside cards become chip rows that wrap or swipe, with scroll-snap and a right-edge mask fade.

Infinite photo strip: a full-width viewport with overflow-x auto, hidden scrollbar, and an edge mask-image linear-gradient(to right, transparent 0, #000 8%, #000 92%, transparent). The track is display flex, width max-content, and animated with translateX(0 to -50%) over calc(count*6s), with the slides duplicated as aria-hidden, inert clones. Slides are clamp(9rem, 42vw, 20rem) wide at aspect-ratio 4/3 with radius 10px. It stays both swipeable (native scroll) and auto-drifting.

Duo grid: FAQ and final CTA share one row on desktop (grid-template-columns 1.3fr 1fr, gap 2rem). The final CTA card is position sticky (top: header + 1rem) beside the long FAQ, and stacks on mobile. The FAQ is native <details>/<summary> in white cards, with a CSS chevron made from a rotated bordered square (45deg to 225deg). The final CTA is a dark gradient card (linear-gradient(160deg, blue-950, blue-800)) with an inverted white button. Rule: .faq[hidden] + .final-cta { grid-column: 1 / -1 }.

Footer: a translucent panel with logos in one row. On desktop it becomes grid auto 1fr, with logos spanning 4 rows on the left and socials, disclaimer and credit stacked on the right. Socials are 48px pill outline links.

Mobile-only sticky bottom CTA bar: position fixed bottom, height calc(3.5rem + safe-bottom), translucent white, slides up from translateY(100%). An IntersectionObserver shows it only after the hero CTA leaves the viewport, and body.has-sticky-bar adds matching padding-bottom so the bar never covers content. It is display none from 768px.

Video modal: native <dialog> with ::backdrop rgba(ink,.82). Width is min(56rem, 100% - 1.5rem, (100svh - 8rem)*16/9) so 16:9 always fits. The stage holds a thumbnail button (hero photo as background, a white round play badge made from an inline SVG data URI). The iframe is injected only on play and removed on close. An 'Open on Drive' fallback link sits below.
Toast: a fixed pill centered at the bottom, placed above the sticky bar on mobile, sliding translate(-50%, 1rem) to 0. It also serves as the share fallback ('Link copied').

Layering: #bg-fallback (static gradient) and canvas#bg3d are fixed at z-index 0 with pointer-events none. Header, main and footer are position relative at z-index 1, so translucent panels show the moving background through them.

effects.name: Inline splash on every load
effects.how: Inline <style id=splash-css> in <head> and a #splash div as the first body child, so it paints with the first byte. It is a fixed full-screen grid over ink #061C47 with a white uppercase title split into two spans. Each span starts at opacity 0 and translateY(.5em) and runs @keyframes splash-in (500ms, cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), second span delayed 120ms). The container runs splash-out (opacity 0, visibility hidden) for 300ms after an 800ms delay. pointer-events: none, so it never blocks input. JS only removes the node on the animationend whose animationName is 'splash-out', with a 1500ms setTimeout fallback. Under reduced motion the spans are static and the fade is 200ms after 600ms. It is aria-hidden.

effects.name: Split-word heading reveal plus soft block reveal
effects.how: JS wraps each word of [data-split] in span.split-word (aria-hidden, style --i=index) and sets aria-label on the heading so screen readers get the full text. The hidden state is gated behind html.js-reveal inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), so content stays visible without JS or with reduced motion. Words start at opacity 0 and translateY(.45em), then transition 450ms with delay min(calc(var(--i)*35ms), 210ms). Hero words run faster (350ms, 30ms stagger, capped at 120ms) so the LCP heading is visible by about 600ms. [data-reveal] blocks start at opacity 0 and translateY(16px) and transition over 500ms. One IntersectionObserver (rootMargin '0px 0px -8% 0px', threshold .05) adds .is-revealed and unobserves, so each element animates once. Afterwards .is-settled drops will-change, set on transitionend or a 1200ms fallback.

effects.name: CSS-only infinite drifting photo strip with pause logic
effects.how: Slides are rendered from images.json as <figure><picture> with AVIF/WebP sources, sizes '(min-width:1024px) 20rem, 42vw' and lazy loading, then the whole set is appended again as clones (aria-hidden, inert, alt ''). The track runs @keyframes strip-drift from translateX(0) to translateX(-50%), linear infinite, over calc(var(--strip-count)*6s). The viewport is a real overflow-x scroller, so touch swipe works natively. Pausing is a class toggle, .is-paused { animation-play-state: paused }, with no per-frame JS. It pauses on mouse pointerenter, pointerdown, touchstart and keyboard focus-visible, and resumes 2500ms after leave, up or blur unless the strip is still hovered or focused. Arrow keys call scrollBy(±0.8*clientWidth, smooth). Under reduced motion there are no clones and no animation, so it is manual swipe only. Edge fade comes from mask-image.

effects.name: Three.js particle wave background with auto-degrade
effects.how: A grid of Points (80x40 on desktop, 48x25 on mobile, jittered) lies on an XZ plane. A custom ShaderMaterial vertex shader displaces y by sin(x*.35+t*.6)*.55 + cos(z*.45+t*.45)*.45 plus per-point aSeed flutter, and passes vMix to mix two brand blues (0x4f9bff to 0x1d6fe8). The fragment shader draws a soft round point via smoothstep(.5,.15,d)*.55 alpha with discard outside the radius. Camera: PerspectiveCamera(55) at (0,7,16) looking at (0,-1,0). Renderer: alpha true, powerPreference low-power, antialias off on mobile, DPR capped at 1.5. Scheduling waits for the first pointerdown/keydown/scroll/touchstart or 3500ms after load, then requestIdleCallback, then dynamic import('./three-subset.js'). Pre-import degrade checks: ?bg=off, reduced motion, hardwareConcurrency<=4, deviceMemory<=4, no WebGL. At runtime it skips 20 warmup frames, measures 90 frames, and on fps<24 (or <30 inside FBAN/FBAV/Instagram UAs) tears down fully (dispose geometry, material and renderer, forceContextLoss) and sets html[data-bg=static]. Mobile is capped at 30fps by skipping frames. It pauses on visibilitychange (resetting the FPS sample), handles webglcontextlost/restored, and debounces resize by 150ms. CSS: the canvas starts at opacity 0 and fades in over 900ms when html[data-bg=3d]. A static radial and linear gradient div always sits underneath as the fallback.

effects.name: Synthesized UI click tick SFX with mute toggle
effects.how: No audio files. AudioContext is created lazily inside the first gesture handler. Each tick is a sine oscillator swept exponentially from 1320Hz to 880Hz over 65ms, with gain falling from 0.05 to 0.0001, and nodes disconnected onended. A delegated capture-phase pointerdown listener on document fires for 'a, button, summary, label, [role=button], .btn', skipping disabled or aria-disabled elements and the toggle itself. A click listener covers keyboard activation (event.detail===0, or no pointerdown in the last 800ms) and resumes the context for iOS. Both listeners are passive and never preventDefault, so navigation is never delayed. The mute state lives in localStorage key 'techrun:muted' with try/catch. The header button carries aria-pressed and swaps inline stroke SVG speaker and speaker-x icons. There is also a CSS-only mask-image speaker fallback while the button is empty.

effects.name: Native CSS custom cursor (no JS follower)
effects.how: Inside @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine), the rule targets html, body, a, button, summary, label, inputs, video, iframe, [role=button], .btn, dialog, .modal *, the carousel elements and details, setting cursor: url(/cursor/cursor-32.svg) 10 5, auto; and then cursor: image-set(url(cursor-32.svg) 1x, url(cursor-64.png) 2x) 10 5, auto. The 32x32 SVG is kept under 2KB with the hotspot at the arrow tip. There is a 'Cursor by Icons8' credit in the footer.

effects.name: Sticky CTA bar via IntersectionObserver
effects.how: It observes the hero CTA and only shows when the CTA is out of view and matchMedia('(max-width:767px)') matches. Showing sets hidden=false, adds body.has-sticky-bar (padding-bottom), and on the next rAF adds .is-visible for the translateY(100%) to 0 plus opacity transition (250ms). Hiding removes the classes and sets hidden after a 250ms timeout. It listens for media query changes.

effects.name: Visibility-aware countdown
effects.how: A single setInterval at 1s formats '12d 04h 09m 33s' with padStart. It runs only while the hero is intersecting and the document is visible, toggled by an IntersectionObserver plus visibilitychange. The aria-label (for example 'Starts in X days...') refreshes once a minute and aria-live is off, so screen readers are not spammed. It switches to 'Event started' and hides when registration is closed.

effects.name: Share with clipboard fallback and toast
effects.how: It uses navigator.share when present and canShare passes, and does nothing on AbortError. Otherwise it tries navigator.clipboard.writeText, then a legacy hidden textarea with execCommand('copy'), then shows a toast: 'Link copied', or the raw URL if copying failed.

effects.name: Lazy video modal
effects.how: Native <dialog>.showModal(). A thumbnail button uses the hero photo as background-image. The Drive iframe (/file/d/{ID}/preview) is created only on play click and removed on close, so it stops loading and playing. There is no autoplay, and an 'Open on Drive' fallback link.

portable_snippets.purpose: Fault-isolated init orchestration plus deferring heavy 3D until interaction or idle
Inline splash that paints with the first byte, faded by CSS only
Split-word and reveal states gated behind a JS class and the reduced-motion media query
Swipeable plus auto-drifting infinite photo strip in pure CSS
Particle wave shaders (two-tone brand mix, soft round points)
Pre-import degrade gate (decide before downloading three)
Synthesized click tick (no audio files)
Native custom cursor scoped to fine pointers
Bottom-anchored photo hero with brand-ink gradient that changes direction at desktop
Build-time config tokens in HTML plus CSS inlining (no render-blocking CSS)

standing_rules: CLAUDE.md is the binding spec, and CONTRACT.md defines file ownership so parallel agents never edit the same file. Each agent edits only its own files and asks the lead for any other change. Agents return a summary under 15 lines with no file dumps.

All content data lives in one JSON config (event.config.json) and is never hardcoded in HTML or JS. Empty values render 'To be announced' or hide the item. Never invent details, prices, dates, sponsors, FAQ answers or testimonials.

Mobile-first for Facebook/Instagram in-app browsers on mid-range Philippine phones over slow connections. Use svh/dvh, never plain 100vh, and respect env(safe-area-inset-*) everywhere (header, sticky bar, container padding).
Palette is limited to the brand hue plus white, expressed as CSS custom properties, and every text/background pair must meet WCAG AA. No colors outside the palette.
One font family only (Poppins), self-hosted WOFF2 with a Latin subset at 400/600/700, font-display swap, preloaded. No Google Fonts request.
Titles sit on one line wherever possible: clamp() sizing tuned for 360px with white-space: nowrap on short headings. Otherwise use text-wrap: balance and never leave an orphan word.
Paragraphs: max-width 60-65ch, line-height 1.6-1.7, text-wrap: pretty, left-aligned, 2 to 4 lines on mobile.
Nothing under 14px anywhere, body at least 16px on mobile, buttons at least 48px tall. No tiny gray text.

Strict page length: about 4 to 5 screens on mobile and 3 to 4 on desktop. Merge sections, keep copy tight (About = 2 to 3 sentences), turn lists into compact 2-column cards or swipe rows. All images move sideways, never stacked vertically.

Motion animates only transform and opacity, 200-600ms, using one easing curve, cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1). Reveals run once via IntersectionObserver. Everything respects prefers-reduced-motion, and content must stay visible without JS or under reduced motion.
Splash shows on every open, lasts about 1 second, is inline HTML/CSS, and is faded by CSS while JS only removes the node. It must not block LCP or cause layout shift.

The 3D background is a fixed canvas with pointer-events none, loaded on idle after first paint. DPR is capped at 1.5, antialias is off on mobile, mobile is capped at 30fps, and it pauses when hidden. It auto-degrades to a static CSS gradient and disposes the renderer on low cores or memory, reduced motion, no WebGL, or low FPS (stricter inside in-app browsers).

SFX: a Web Audio synthesized tick (50-80ms) on every click or tap. The AudioContext is created only after the first gesture, volume is low, and a mute toggle is saved in localStorage inside try/catch. Audio must never delay navigation.

Custom cursor uses the native CSS cursor only, never a JS follower. It is scoped to (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine), explicitly covers links, buttons, summary, label, video, modal and carousel, and uses a 32px SVG under 2KB plus a 64px PNG for 2x. Credit Icons8 in the footer at 14px or larger.

Every localStorage or sessionStorage access is wrapped in try/catch, and every feature degrades gracefully: navigator.share falls back to clipboard plus toast, an .ics download falls back to Google Calendar, an embed failure falls back to an 'Open on' link.
Each init function is wrapped so it never throws into main.js and tolerates missing DOM nodes. Inits must be idempotent.

Performance budget (mobile Lighthouse): Performance at least 90 (aim for 95+), A11y, Best Practices and SEO at least 95. LCP under 2.5s, INP under 200ms, CLS under 0.1, TBT under 200ms, FCP under 1.8s. Initial transfer under about 500KB. Images as AVIF/WebP with srcset and explicit width/height, hero preloaded with fetchpriority high, everything else lazy. Critical CSS inlined, no render-blocking resources. If an effect costs the budget, simplify or cut it and say so.

Third-party embeds (video iframes, Pixel) load only on demand: the iframe is injected only when the modal opens and removed on close, the Pixel loads on idle or first interaction, and tracking never delays link opening or calls preventDefault.
CTA links get target=_blank rel=noopener plus UTM params, and incoming utm_* and fbclid params pass through (incoming values win). A config flag switches every CTA to a disabled 'closed' state.

SEO and a11y basics: title, meta description, OG and Twitter tags, canonical, favicon from the logo, semantic landmarks, a skip link, alt text everywhere, visible focus-visible outlines (3px, offset 3px, lighter outline color on dark sections), aria-label on split headings.
Git: conventional commits, push to main, never force-push or rewrite history. Never commit secrets, .env, node_modules, raw originals (assets-raw) or files over 50MB, and no video files in the repo.
Do not: add forms or payment flows, use stock photos in place of real ones without saying so, build a JS cursor, use off-palette colors or other fonts, or let parallel agents edit the same file.

Global user preference (from ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md): no hyphens or dashes before text and no decorative leading lines in front of labels. Write eyebrow labels as plain text ('WHO WE ARE', '01') and avoid em dashes in UI copy.

project: Theoraux website (C:\Theoraux\website). Next.js 16 software studio site, the author's own agency brand.
stack: Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4 (@theme inline in src/app/globals.css, class based dark mode via @custom-variant dark), GSAP 3 + ScrollTrigger (dynamically imported, only when a section is within 2000px), Three.js 0.184 (home story logo GLB plus a WebGL glyph shader in the CTA), framer-motion being phased out in favour of CSS, lucide-react icons, next/font/google, Web Audio API synthesized SFX (no audio files), sharp scripts for WebP/OG images, node --test unit tests, playwright-core e2e crawl. Nearly every effect is pure CSS keyframes plus one shared IntersectionObserver, so it ports directly to Vite + vanilla JS + plain CSS.
visual_signature: Strict monochrome. Pure #000 and #fff with neutral greys (#0a0a0a surface, #262626 dark border, #e5e5e5 light border, muted text neutral-600 light and neutral-400 dark, #626262 and #a3a3a3 in the story CSS). Dark is the default theme: the inline head script adds .dark unless localStorage.theme is 'light'. Selection colours invert (black bg and white text in light mode, the reverse in dark). Colour appears only as rare accents: a pencil blue (#244877 light, #a8c9ee dark) for the technical sketch chapter, a blue (#245bc9 to rgb .18,.43,1.0) tint in the ASCII glyph field, and one conic rainbow edge glow (#4985ff, #8e61ed, #dd63c8, #fa845b, #edc974, #75cadd) used in a single scroll chapter only. Type, with exact weights: display headings in Manrope 300 only, forced with `.font-display{font-weight:300!important}`. Big display sizes run text-6xl/7xl/8xl, leading 0.98 to 1.05, tracking tight, with story and CTA headlines at letter-spacing -0.055em and clamp(48px,5.4vw,104px). Wordmark, eyebrows and loader labels use Jost 300, uppercase, 10 to 11px, tracking 0.16em to 0.32em (eyebrow standard is 10px at 0.25em; the wordmark is 0.3em). Body is Inter, with italics synthesized on purpose. Small numeric labels use IBM Plex Mono 400 uppercase 10px at 0.2em to 0.25em, or text-sm for index numbers like "01". Layout: max-w-7xl container with px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8. Sections use py-20 to py-32 and are flat, with no cards-on-gradients. Edges are 1px hairlines (black/10, white/10, black/15 on list tops), and some rules are full bleed (`.full-bleed` uses the --sbw scrollbar width). Corners are square almost everywhere (only `rounded` 4px on buttons and cards). Images are grayscale by default and turn to colour on hover. Navigation uses plain arrows (→ and ↗) that nudge translate-x-1 on hover. Two-digit zero-padded index numbers ("01") label lists. Why it does not look like a template: the restraint (one weight per family), the editorial label system, paragraphs with designed line silhouettes (taper or diamond line breaks computed per paragraph), every visible parenthetical set in italic, the pipe separator "Software Studio | Available Worldwide", synthesized tactile sounds on clicks and on text animations, a canvas wave band at the foot of every hero, and full-viewport closing CTAs over an animated ASCII glyph field.
layout_patterns: Hero (Hero.tsx): section min-h-[92vh] flex column justify-between, pt-36. A Jost uppercase label (11 to 13px, tracking 0.22 to 0.3em) types in with a caret. The h1 is in Manrope 300, text-6xl to 8xl, leading 0.98, split across two lines with \n, and each word drops in. The lead paragraph sits in a wrapper set to `w-max max-w-full` with the paragraph at `w-0 min-w-full`, so the paragraph is exactly as wide as the longest headline line. Two square outline buttons are joined edge to edge (the second gets -ml-px, hover:z-10), with border black/30 that turns to a solid black fill with white text on hover. The animated wave canvas band takes the bottom clamp(160px,28vh,300px), and the section reserves that height plus 1.5rem as bottom padding so the wave never overlaps text.

Sticky heading plus indexed list (ServicesSection.tsx): a 12-column grid. The left col-span-4 is `lg:sticky lg:top-32` and holds the eyebrow, the title, the description and an underline-sweep link. The right col-span-8 is a `ul` with border-t black/15, and each `li` has border-b black/10. Each row is a link laid out as grid-cols-[2.5rem_15rem_1fr_auto]: mono index '01', a display h3 that moves translate-x-1 on hover, a short description, and a '→' at the end. Row hover is bg-black/[0.02].

Two-column offer teaser (LaunchSprintTeaser.tsx): the left col-span-7 has the section header and a solid lg button. The right col-span-5 is a bordered box (border black/15, divide-y black/10) holding three big statement rows. Each row has a display text-3xl phrase with a count-up number on the left and a mono 10px index '01' on the right, aligned on the baseline with justify-between.

Process (Process.tsx + process.css): a top grid of 2 columns, with the section header on the left and a short paragraph plus link on the right, aligned with items-end. Below them is a full-bleed 1px rule, then a 4-column step grid. Each step has a 1px grey border-top, and a ::before 2px currentColor bar grows across it with scaleX(var(--step-progress)). The step number sits in a 38x32 bordered box that inverts (filled black, white text) once data-reached. Steps rise from translateY(44px) scale(.97) opacity .8, driven by scroll scrub.

Closing CTA (CTABanner.tsx): min-h-[100svh], centered. An animated ASCII glyph field (SymbolField) fills the background, with a radial-gradient ellipse at 45% by 42% of paper colour (alpha 0.9) behind the text so the copy stays legible. The headline is 5xl to 6rem, font-light, tracking -0.055em, word drop, and wrapped in a link. Below it sits one solid button.

Pinned scroll story (HomeStory + home-story.css): a section 850svh tall with a sticky 100svh viewport (overflow: clip). It runs four chapters that are absolutely stacked and crossfade by scroll progress. Chapters alternate sides: on left chapters the headline sits bottom-left (width 47%, bottom 7%, left 4vw) and the support copy bottom-right (width 27%); right chapters mirror this. A chapter index shows top-right in Jost 11px. A topline is set at top:108px. Data attributes on the root (data-chapter, data-stage, data-mode) drive the CSS. On mobile, chapters stack at the bottom with env(safe-area-inset-bottom). Static fallback: plain stacked chapters at 90svh.

Loader (story-loader): a fixed fullscreen paper panel. The Jost wordmark sits at top-left (top 40px, left 4vw, 20px, tracking 0.3em). In the centre is a Manrope 300 84px percentage with a small 22px '%'. Under it, a 1px progress track (currentColor at 15% via color-mix) is filled by a scaleX bar. A Skip button sits bottom-right and a note bottom-left, both in Jost 11px uppercase.

Portfolio orbit (story-work): project cards move along a diagonal path (from upper-left, growing toward the centre, then shrinking off to the lower-right), with at most 3 visible. A fixed caption column sits at the left (top 44%, width min(24vw,300px)), and its project details crossfade. The footer holds numbered step buttons (44px min) and an 'All projects' link. Image grayscale is driven by a CSS variable: filter: grayscale(calc(1 - var(--work-focus))).

Marquee of testimonial or people cards (ClientsNetworkMarquee + .people-marquee): square bordered cards w-[min(82vw,22rem)] min-h-72 with a mono 10px kind label, a display name, an italic quote, and a border-t footer link. The track is duplicated and animates translateX(-50%). The edges fade with mask-image linear-gradient(to right, transparent, #000 3%, #000 97%, transparent). It pauses on hover, on focus-within, when offscreen (IO) and in hidden tabs. On mobile, coarse pointers and reduced motion it becomes a native scroll-snap swipe row and the duplicate is hidden.

Navbar: fixed, transparent until scrollY > 20, then border-b black/10, bg-white/90 and backdrop-blur-md. Logo mark on the left. Links are Manrope uppercase 13px with tracking 0.08em, and active state uses an ::after 1px underline at bottom 1.5. On the right sits a two-icon theme group (sun and moon, aria-pressed) and an outline 'Let's Talk →' button. Mobile gets a fullscreen sheet with text-3xl links, Escape closes it, and body scroll is locked.

Footer: a 12-column grid. Col 5 holds the Jost wordmark (tracking 0.3em) with a tagline and social icons. The other columns are separated by md:border-l black/10 with pl-8, and each has a Jost uppercase column label (a

, not a heading) over link-underline links set to leading-none.
Case study pages: hero, facts strip, cover, results, story, then one connected footer bar with previous, the CTA and next. Results are sorted by magnitude and their numbers count up.

effects.name: Word drop headline (DropText)
effects.how:
The HTML splits the headline into words, each wrapped as (plain spaces between them,
for \n). The parent gets data-fx="drop". The keyframe fx-drop goes from opacity 0 and translateY(-0.5em) to none, 0.5s ease-out, with animation-delay calc(min(var(--i),8)*60ms) so the stagger is capped at 8 words. Above the fold the class fx-load uses a softer variant (from opacity .88, translateY(-.2em)) so the LCP text paints right away. Below the fold, JS adds .fx-pending (words at opacity 0) and then .fx-in when the element intersects. All of it sits inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), and nothing is hidden when JS is off.

effects.name: Typewriter label with caret (TypeText)
effects.how: Applies only to labels of 38 characters or fewer on a single line. The parent has --n set to the character count and an inner .fx-t (inline-block, nowrap). The animation is clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0), running calc(var(--n)*35ms) with steps(var(--n),end). For proportional fonts (.fx-prop, width fit-content) the caret is an ::after with inset:0 and border-right 1px currentColor, animated translateX(-100%) to 0 with the same steps so it tracks the clip edge. It blinks 3 times (0.5s steps(1)) and then fades out once typing ends. For mono fonts the caret moves by calc(var(--n)*(1ch + var(--fx-ls))).

effects.name: Count up numbers
effects.how: The server HTML shows the final text. .fx-count is an inline-grid whose ::after has content: attr(data-t), stacked in the same grid cell, visibility hidden and height 0, which reserves the final width so nothing shifts (tabular-nums). On intersect, a single rAF loop rewrites textContent from 0 to the value with easeOutCubic over 1200ms, keeping the prefix and suffix ('₱', '%', '+', K/M). Years from 1900 to 2100 and integers below 10 do not count unless they opt in.

effects.name: Single shared FX controller
effects.how: One IntersectionObserver (rootMargin '0px 0px -8% 0px') and one rAF loop serve every [data-fx] element. On load it reads all rects in one batch first, then writes classes: elements already above the viewport settle immediately, elements within 95% of the viewport keep their final state, and only elements below the fold get .fx-pending and are observed. The whole controller is skipped under reduced motion.

effects.name: Reveal on scroll
effects.how: Pending state: .reveal-pending {opacity:.8; transform:translateY(16px); transition: opacity .5s, transform .5s}, and .reveal-in sets opacity 1 and transform none. The starting opacity is .8 rather than 0 so text caught mid-fade still passes AA contrast. JS adds pending only to nodes below 95% of the viewport, with a batched read-then-write queue (queueMicrotask). Stagger comes from an inline transitionDelay of (index%4)*50ms or (index%2)*80ms.

effects.name: Animated wave band canvas (FlowBackground)
effects.how: A 2D canvas pinned to the bottom of each hero. It draws 18 sine lines (12 under 640px). Line i has baseY = h*(0.28 + p*0.68) and y = baseY + sin(nx*6 + t*0.00022 + i*0.35)*(22+p*20) + sin(nx*13 + t*0.00022*1.7 + i*0.5)*(9+p*9). Opacity is 0.55 with lineWidth 1.4 for the top ridge, and 0.34 - p*0.2 for the rest. About 170 random dots of radius 0.3 to 1.3 sit at 0.16 to 0.18 alpha. The soft shadow under the ridge is drawn on a canvas at 1/8 size with a vertical alpha gradient and then upscaled, which replaces a costly blur. The canvas is masked with linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent 0%, black 22%, black 88%, transparent 100%). Frames are capped near 30fps (30ms interval). The loop pauses via IntersectionObserver and visibilitychange, re-renders on theme change through a MutationObserver on html class, and draws a single frame under reduced motion. DPR is capped at 2. It mounts after requestIdleCallback.

effects.name: ASCII glyph field (SymbolField)
effects.how: A WebGL fullscreen quad with a glyph atlas texture of 5 symbols '.:-+*'. The fragment shader quantizes the screen into 12px cells and computes an fbm noise flow field plus a sin stream and fold. A pointer ripple sin(dist*32 - t*2)*exp(-dist*7) is added. The resulting signal picks the glyph index floor(signal*5), and the colour mixes grey toward blue. A wave envelope and a centre fade keep the middle clear for the CTA text. On mobile and with Save-Data, the fallback is a static SVG of <text> rows of the same symbols, masked by thick white bezier strokes and filled with a linear gradient from currentColor .68 to #245bc9. A vanilla port could use a 2D canvas with fillText per cell if WebGL is too heavy.

effects.name: Scroll scrubbed process steps
effects.how: GSAP ScrollTrigger on the step track (start 'top 80%', end 'bottom 35%', scrub 0.65) tweens a dummy {progress} from 0 to 1. Each step's local value is clamp((progress - i*0.25)/0.25), smoothstepped as l*l*(3-2l). It then sets transform translate3d(0,(1-e)*44px,0) scale(.97+e*.03), opacity .8+e*.2, the CSS var --step-progress (driving the ::before bar scaleX), and data-reached once local >= .5 (which inverts the number box). A rising 'poink' sound plays as each step is reached. GSAP is imported only when an IO with rootMargin 2000px fires. In vanilla JS a scroll listener computing progress from getBoundingClientRect, with lerp smoothing, would do the same.

effects.name: Circular theme reveal
effects.how: Clicking a theme button stores clientX/Y in --theme-x/--theme-y on html, then calls document.startViewTransition(applyTheme). CSS sets ::view-transition-old(root){animation:none} and ::view-transition-new(root){animation: theme-reveal .6s ease-in-out; clip-path: circle(0% at var(--theme-x) var(--theme-y))}, animating to circle(150%). Without support, or under reduced motion, the theme swaps instantly.

effects.name: Splash wordmark intro
effects.how: A fixed fullscreen overlay at z 200 in the theme paper colour, already present in the server HTML. The wordmark is Jost 300 uppercase, clamp(2rem,7vw,5.5rem), tracking 0.32em, with pl-[0.32em] to optically centre it. Each letter is a span using splash-letter (from opacity 0 and translate3d(0,.35em,0), 0.5s cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1), delay 80ms + i*45ms). The overlay runs splash-out over 1.7s (opacity held until 58.8%, then fading to 0) plus a separate 0s splash-hide that sets visibility hidden at 1.7s, so it never blocks input. It is display:none under reduced motion. No JS is involved.

effects.name: Underline sweep links
effects.how: .link-underline{background-image:linear-gradient(currentColor,currentColor);background-repeat:no-repeat;background-position:0 100%;background-size:0% 1px;padding-bottom:3px;transition:background-size .35s cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1)}. On hover (gated by @media (hover:hover)) and on :focus-visible the size becomes 100% 1px. Project titles use the same technique inline.

effects.name: Grayscale to colour cover hover
effects.how: The image starts grayscale. On group-hover it becomes grayscale-0 with scale 1.03 over a 500ms ease-out transition. The border goes from black/10 to black/40, the arrow ↗ moves -translate-y-0.5 and translate-x-0.5, and the title's underline sweep runs.

effects.name: Rainbow edge glow chapter
effects.how: A fixed overlay with opacity var(--story-glow) holds a frame inset -16px with padding 28px. The frame is masked as a ring using mask: linear-gradient(#fff 0 0) content-box, linear-gradient(#fff 0 0) with mask-composite: exclude. Inside it, a conic-gradient spectrum at inset -40% rotates by var(--story-glow-turn), set from scroll, and also runs a 14s loop of translate, rotate and hue-rotate. A halo copy with blur(18px) sits beneath. animation-play-state is paused unless data-motion=running.

effects.name: Synthesized UI sounds (sfx)
effects.how: Uses Web Audio only. A click is a bandpass-filtered white noise burst (about 4kHz, Q .9, exponential decay 15ms) plus a sine thump sweeping 220 to 90Hz over 25ms. A primary-button click is deeper (3.3kHz noise, 180 to 70Hz). Releasing the click plays a quieter echo at 40% gain and slightly higher pitch. Key clack: 3kHz noise for 10ms plus a 160 to 100Hz thock. Heading drop: 4 to 6 keys spaced 35 to 50ms apart with falling gain, ending on an 'enter' key. Poink: a sine bending f*0.8 to f*1.35 over 130ms plus a triangle overtone, with pitch rising by step. Master gain is 0.2 and a voice budget caps playback at 12 voices per second. The AudioContext unlocks on the first gesture, and sound is off by default under reduced motion. A global delegated pointerdown and keydown listener maps elements to a sound variant (via data-sfx attributes, tag and role).

effects.name: Paragraph silhouettes (ShapedText)
effects.how: After document.fonts.ready, the client measures words with canvas measureText using the computed font, then runs a DP over line breaks that minimizes RMS error against a target width profile: taper for left-aligned text, diamond for centred text. The chosen lines render as block spans, a ResizeObserver reflows them, and the SSR HTML keeps the full plain text. Gates: off below 230px width, off above 100 words, and off for narrow columns with 7 or more lines. Above-the-fold paragraphs keep their natural line count to avoid CLS. A lighter vanilla port: compute greedy lines for progressively narrower max widths per line.

standing_rules: No hyphens or dashes in visible copy, matching the user's global CLAUDE.md. Hyphenated words become two words ('fixed price', 'Philippines based'). Em and en dashes are reworded with a comma, colon or period. Ranges use 'to' ('₱8,000 to ₱15,000'). No decorative leading rules before eyebrows ('01' not '01 —'). Hyphens in code, slugs and class names are fine.
Use ' | ' (a pipe with a space on each side) as the visible separator instead of '/', for example 'Software Studio | Available Worldwide' and 'Slack | Viber'. The exception is 'UI & UX'.

All visible text inside parentheses, the parentheses included, is italic. Metadata, alt text, aria labels, <option> text and JSON-LD stay plain. Phone groups like '(+63)' are an exception and stay upright.

No invented claims, awards, superlatives or fake testimonials. Captions state only what is shown. No countdown timers or live scarcity counts (static 'N slots per month' only). Internal tier prices are never published ('Inquire for a fixed quote').

Typography discipline: one weight per family. Manrope 300 for display (forced with !important), Jost 300 uppercase tracked for the wordmark, eyebrows and labels (10px, 0.25em), Inter for body with synthesized italics, IBM Plex Mono 400 for small numeric labels. The author does not drift to other display fonts.

Monochrome black and white with hairline 1px borders at 10 to 15% alpha, square corners, grayscale imagery that colours on hover. Colour accents are rare and purposeful, limited to one chapter or one effect.
Dark theme by default, with a light toggle saved to localStorage and an inline head script to avoid flash. Every visual is checked in both themes at about 1440px and 400px.

Motion is progressive enhancement: content is visible without JS, pending styles are added only by JS, and everything is gated behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference. Only opacity, transform and clip-path animate. Reveal starts at opacity .8 rather than 0 to keep AA contrast. Above-the-fold text never starts hidden, protecting LCP.

Performance: one shared IntersectionObserver and rAF for all text FX. Batch layout reads before writes. Cap canvas at about 30fps and DPR 2. Pause loops when offscreen (IO) and when the tab is hidden (visibilitychange). Lighter density under 640px. Lazy-import heavy libraries (GSAP, three) only near use. Save-Data and mobile get static fallbacks. Dispose renderers, observers and listeners. Target CLS 0.
Decorative layers never overlap text or buttons: the hero reserves the wave band height as bottom padding. Glows sit behind a radial paper-colour scrim for legibility.

Accessibility: a skip link to main, focus-visible outlines of 2px currentColor with offset 2 to 8px, 44px minimum touch targets, aria-pressed theme buttons, a mobile menu that closes on Escape and locks scroll, marquees that pause on hover and focus and become native swipe rows on touch, and duplicate marquee items with tabIndex -1.
Hover effects are gated with @media (hover: hover). The custom cursor and hover sweeps apply to fine pointers only, and touch keeps native behaviour.

Sound: synthesized Web Audio clicks, key clacks on headline drops and typing, and a rising 'poink' for steps. Master gain is low (0.2), limited to 12 voices per second, unlocked on the first gesture, off under reduced motion, with no audio files. The splash intro plays on every full load (CSS only, about 1.7s, never blocks input).
Glass utilities avoid backdrop-filter (only the scrolled navbar uses backdrop-blur). The idle shine sweep is used on only one CTA per page.
No horizontal overflow: html overflow-x: clip (not hidden, so sticky and pins still work) and full-bleed rules use the --sbw scrollbar width.

SEO is never weakened: metadata, canonicals, JSON-LD and the sitemap are kept, and server HTML holds the full text even when the client reshapes it. Workflow: surgical edits, no commits until the owner says so, a build plus an e2e crawl that scrolls every page before shipping, and DOM-moving animation code cleaned up synchronously.

effects.name: Word-by-word heading reveal
effects.how: Split the heading text on whitespace into <span class='word' style='--i:N'>, with N counting up across nested elements so a span.g inside keeps the sequence. CSS: .word{display:inline-block;opacity:0;transform:translateY(.5em);transition:opacity .6s ease,transform .6s ease;transition-delay:calc(var(--i)*35ms)}. When the ancestor .rv gets .in, set .word{opacity:1;transform:none}. Only opacity and transform are animated (blur was removed for repaint cost). In vanilla JS, walk the text nodes of [data-words] elements once on load and wrap each word.

effects.name: Scroll reveal
effects.how: .rv{opacity:0;transform:translateY(26px);transition:opacity .7s ease,transform .7s ease} .rv.in{opacity:1;transform:none}. One IntersectionObserver at threshold 0.12 adds 'in' and then unobserves. The reduced-motion override shows everything immediately. Never apply it to the LCP hero image.

effects.name: Count-up counters
effects.how: An IntersectionObserver at threshold 0.5 fires once and runs a rAF loop over 1400ms with easeOutCubic (1-(1-p)^3), rendering prefix + Math.round(to*eased) + suffix. Under reduced motion it jumps straight to the final value.

effects.name: Drifting liquid orbs background
effects.how: A fixed .bg-field (z-index 0, pointer-events none) holds 3 absolutely positioned circles: radial-gradient lime .34, blue .55 and green2 .22, each fading to 0 at about 68%. filter:blur(48px), mix-blend-mode:screen, sizes 62vw/64vw/42vw, positioned partly off-screen. Keyframes orbA/B/C translate a few vw and scale .94 to 1.16 over 24s, 28s and 20s ease-in-out infinite. Mobile uses blur 30px and smaller orbs. Reduced motion stops the animation. Content (main, header, footer) sits at position:relative;z-index:1.

effects.name: WebGL market-lines background with cursor glow
effects.how: A fixed .mkt-bg div at z-index -1 has a CSS 'poster' background (radial lime glow at the bottom, blue vertical fade, repeating 72px faint lime horizontal rules). After window load AND the first real input (pointermove, pointerdown, touchstart, scroll, wheel or keydown; no timer fallback, so Lighthouse never loads it), it dynamically imports three. It is skipped when saveData is on, deviceMemory <= 2 or hardwareConcurrency <= 2, and draws one still frame under reduced motion. Scene: 9 lines (6 on touch) of 120 LineSegments each plus 12 Points, AdditiveBlending, and clip-space shaders with no camera math. The vertex shader builds a jagged price-chart curve from 3 octaves of value noise that scrolls sideways (speed 0.1 to 0.2 per line) plus a sine sway, and lifts y near 6 pointer-trail uniforms with an exp(-d²/0.075) falloff. Slot 0 is an eased hover head that stays lit while the pointer is over the page. Color alternates line by line between lime and lightened blue, with lime under the glow. Line alpha is 0.34 times an edge fade. Frame caps are 45fps while active (30 on touch) and 12fps idle, with a full pause after 20s without input, plus pause when hidden or off-screen. The canvas fades in over .6s via .is-live. Colors are read from the CSS vars --green and --blue.

effects.name: Liquid sheen on every glass card
effects.how: Card gets position:relative;isolation:isolate. ::before covers inset:0 with border-radius:inherit and background linear-gradient(120deg, rgba(255,255,255,.18) 0%, transparent 24%, rgba(192,240,48,.12) 50%, rgba(1,40,169,.12) 66%, transparent 100%), background-size 260%, animation liquidSheen 11s ease-in-out infinite (background-position 0% 15% to 100% 85%), opacity .85, and a per-card --shine-delay. Children get z-index:1. A perf note in the docs: this was about 85% of the render CPU, so pause it offscreen or limit how many cards carry it.

standing_rules: No em dashes, or en dashes used as sentence punctuation, anywhere in user-facing copy (house rule across all GN sites; GN Academy enforces it with a test). The global user rule adds: no leading dashes or decorative rules before labels or eyebrows (write 'WHO WE ARE', not '—— WHO WE ARE' or '01 —').

Bright glassmorphism, not murky glass: translucent gradient over the brand tokens, backdrop-filter blur() saturate(), a top-edge inset highlight, shadows tinted toward the brand color. Reuse existing brand tokens rather than inventing new hex values.

A continuous subtle shine or shimmer sweep on glass surfaces and buttons, using an overlay or soft-light blend so it can only lighten. Pure CSS. Freeze it to a static highlight under prefers-reduced-motion and give a solid fallback under prefers-reduced-transparency.
